evidence_finding: Across 35 citizen engagement programmes in low- and middle-income countries, direct engagement between users and providers often improved access and service quality, but not wellbeing without supply-side support; pressing politicians to hold providers accountable usually did not change services.
evidence_basis: abstract: meta-analysis and framework synthesis of 35 programmes; direct user-provider engagement improves access and quality; complementary interventions needed; political pressure route usually ineffective.
